_comment: Binds each deletion_rules.csv condition, by SHA-256 of its whitespace-normalised casefolded wording, to a predicate in conditions.py. A changed or new condition has no binding and evaluates UNKNOWN. on_false states the consequence when the predicate is evidenced FALSE: TARGET_SATISFIED (the condition is the identifiability that the action removes), DEFAULT_ERASURE (an exemption from the authorised deletion does not apply), or UNRESOLVED (no supplied rule decides).

anonymization._comment: F-02 (pre-M9). Rule 07/08 'still attributable' is FALSE only when an ANONYMIZE_RECORD operation on the same system/resource (a claim) is independently corroborated by a later source read whose identifier columns are removed, with no indirect identifier and no later copy naming the subject. Explicitly null identifier columns alone are DIRECT_REMOVED (UNKNOWN). Indirect identifiers re-link (TRUE) only when their value co-occurs with the subject's direct identifiers in another admissible record.
anonymization._nesting: Indirect, direct and stable-reference fields are found at any depth of nested objects and arrays (and embedded record_json); a field matches by exact name or by a '_<name>' suffix (e.g. source_session_id). Only text/integer values count; booleans, floats and unnamed numbers are never identities.

_retention_without_period_comment: Rule 12 when no retention period is supplied. 'unknown' keeps the condition UNKNOWN (no treatment decided). 'retain_observed_without_period' preserves an observed, subject-attributed security audit record because deletion_rules.csv has no rule that authorizes deleting SECURITY_AUDIT_LOG. Expired periods are never retained.
_support_without_content_comment: RELAXED experiment: Rule 05 with no observable conversation content takes the REDACT branch ('unknown' keeps it UNKNOWN).
